analysis: Both units are head_text excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 41545-43452), a golden-vector test fixture for the prompt contract (request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan with chain hashes, token_ids). The patch excerpt shows the changes: an added "additional_context": {"enable_thinking": false} in a template_input, and updated prompt_token_count, chain_hash and token_ids values. In the visible excerpt (tool-turn, responses endpoint, exact_block_multiple, gemma, gemma_tool_turn vectors), the data is synthetic (weather, 'x x x', 'summarize'), with no secrets, credentials, keys, attestation material or real consumer content. The fixture is data only: it creates no executable surface, no auth/attestation change, and no change to the TB-002 or TB-009 gates, WebSocket contract, key custody or encryption handling. The prompt_contract_id in the visible vectors is 507d6d7a..., while the patch excerpt's older hunk shows 8171fec3... for a different vector; I could not see the consumers (the Go coordinator and Swift provider prompt-planning code), so whether all implementations compute the new contract id and chain hashes consistently is outside the supplied evidence. A mismatch would be a cache-key and correctness concern for prefix-cache keying (T-041), not a demonstrated vulnerability. Remaining integration questions: confirm the Go and Swift prompt-contract code is updated in this PR in step with these vectors, and that the token-id and chain-hash changes do not weaken cross-tenant prefix-cache scoping (scope_id 'fixture-scope' is retained). No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied units.
